bull_case: Meta combines a 3.6B-person daily network, global advertiser demand and AI-driven ranking/monetization at a scale few peers can match. The core ad engine is still growing both impressions and price.
bear_case: Revenue remains overwhelmingly advertising-driven, while younger-user competition, regulation and platform shifts can hit the same demand engine across multiple apps. Starting scale also limits category growth.
thesis: Meta is a structural leader in global social discovery and performance advertising. Scale, distribution and AI-enhanced monetization support durable category leadership, but the business still has one dominant final demand engine: advertising. Under the harness durability-risks observable, that concentration caps the diversification score at 45. Leadership is therefore strong, not fully diversified.

evidence.claim: FY2025 advertising revenue was $196.18B of $200.97B total revenue, up 22% YoY; ad impressions rose 12% and average price per ad rose 9%.
Family daily active people averaged 3.60B in June 2026, while Q2 ad impressions grew 14% and price per ad 12% YoY.
Family of Apps generated $102.47B of 2025 operating income at a 52% operating margin, demonstrating category-scale economics even while Reality Labs lost $19.19B.

Meta's 10-K explicitly identifies intense competition for users, advertisers, developers and frontier AI, including weaker engagement in some demographics; this is the main structural counterweight to scale.

counterevidence: Advertising represented roughly 98% of 2025 revenue, so independent final-market diversification is limited despite multiple apps.
Meta itself reports stronger competition among younger users and lower monetization on Reels than Feed/Stories.
AI leadership is contested by other frontier-model developers and hyperscalers with comparable capital access.
Regulatory restrictions can affect targeting, data use, app distribution or monetization across multiple products simultaneously.
unknowns: Meta does not disclose advertiser concentration or wallet share in a way that permits a clean cross-platform switching-cost estimate.
The long-run revenue contribution of subscriptions, business messaging, AI agents and Reality Labs remains too small or insufficiently disclosed to count as separate >10% final markets.
falsifiers: Family DAP declines for multiple quarters while ad impressions and price per ad also weaken.
Advertising growth falls structurally below global digital-ad growth without offsetting new revenue pools.
A regulatory or platform-access shock causes sustained double-digit FoA revenue decline.

key_kpis.name: Ad impressions + price per ad
key_kpis.threshold: combined monetization growth remains clearly positive

key_kpis.name: Non-ad revenue share
key_kpis.threshold: move toward a decision-useful second revenue engine

next_checks: Track Threads, WhatsApp, subscriptions and enterprise AI as potential independent demand engines.
Compare Meta ad growth with global digital-ad growth to distinguish category growth from share gain.
Reassess durability after major privacy, app-distribution or AI regulatory changes.

subscores.rationale: Long-term demand and willingness to pay are demonstrated by 22% FY2025 ad growth and continued Q2 2026 growth in both impressions and pricing. This fits the 75 anchor; concentration and regulation prevent 90.

Meta operates at 3.60B Family DAP with >$196B annual advertising revenue and a 52% FoA operating margin. Multiple primary metrics establish category leadership; competition from Google/TikTok and frontier-AI peers prevents a 90.
The observable rubric assigns 45 when a single demand driver accounts for >=80% of revenue. Advertising was about 98% of FY2025 revenue, so multiple apps do not qualify as independent final markets.

uncertainties.rationale: Advertising demand is well evidenced, but the exact 5-10 year effect of AI-mediated discovery is still evolving.
Scale is clear; relative share against other ad platforms is not frozen in the run.
New revenue pools exist but are not yet large enough to reduce the observable advertising-concentration penalty.
